title: The Idran
summary: The mage cult behind the True Hand.

claims.text: About 3,000 years ago a cult of mages came to the Middle East; an Egyptian immortal, Inauhaten, led them into the Underworld to a sunless city and gave them the Guarded Rubrics.
Strictly, Tal'Mahe'Ra names the Idran cult after it took up Enochian eschatology, and Black Hand names the Cainite sect serving its aims; most use the two loosely.
The cult grew from a war in the Himalayas between Eastern sages who sought to step off the Wheel and Western mortuary priests who held even corpses holy.

title: The Guarded Rubrics
summary: The Idran's scripture of the end.

claims.text: The Rubrics share topics and some text with Noddist writings but look to the end rather than the beginning; one sign of the end is Caine's brood returning to Enoch.
Those who hold Enoch, the cult believes, steer the apocalypse; only beings touched by both life and death can take hold of it.
The yamasattva keep key passages hidden for fear of how the Hand might act on them.

title: The Eastern and Western Hands
summary: The first Cainite allies of the cult.

claims.text: From about 800 BCE the cult courted the Salubri and the Assamites in the East; both refused the idea of bringing Gehenna but kept fighting the Followers of Set.
It later reached the True Brujah, the Old Clan Tzimisce and a line of outcast Ventrue later called the Danava, who formed the Western Hand.
After a cabal diablerized the Lasombra founder, Roderigo al-Dakhil urged the Hand to steer the rebels rather than destroy them, tying its fate to the young Sabbat.
Roderigo later reported a Black Hand inside the Sabbat and claimed both its name and its founding.
The Sabbat's tattoo is a plain black crescent; the True Hand's adds the eclipse.

title: The Del'Roh
summary: War leader and ruler of the Hand.

claims.text: The reunited Hand chose Anadja as war leader, taking a title from old Ghemalish meaning to serve; the campaign to retake Enoch took three years, the assault itself only two nights.
The Del'Roh is the only vampire to approach the Basalt Throne of Caine and keep both sanity and unlife.
The Del'Roh claims to commune nightly with the Aralu Nergal while dreaming.
After the Fifth Maelstrom the sect stagnated; its narrow entry rules left it near irrelevance as the Camarilla and Sabbat grew.
The seraphim in conclave ended the old limits and began to recruit every Clan save the Tzimisce and the Followers of Set, to loud protest from younger members.
Members guess the sect at anything from 400 to over 1,500, not counting mortal servants; even titled members rarely know the truth of Enoch or the Aralu.

title: Initiation Rites
summary: How recruits join the True Hand.

claims.text: In one rite the recruit guards a chosen mortal for seven nights, then must get that mortal to aid after a staged attack without feeding or giving vitae.

In the Rite of the Antediluvians the recruit bears the supervising mentor's Clan curse for a month as well as their own; mentors are mostly Malkavian, Nosferatu or Ventrue and never share the recruit's Clan.
The Rite of Sak Yant carves a black crescent with an eclipse into the palm; vitae alone cannot heal it, and only Hand members, or anyone in the Shadowlands, can see it.
Specters hunt those who bear the mark, and legend says it leaves them open to the yamasattva's control.

title: The Wazir and the Palm
summary: How the True Hand is ruled.

claims.text: Ten seraphim serve the Del'Roh as lieutenants, ranked by their cover identities in other sects; with three undead magi called the yamasattva together these thirteen sit as a tribunal.
With the Del'Roh, that tribunal is the Wazir, which sets doctrine; below it dominions captain missions or infiltration, then the Cult of the Erinyes.
The Non-Aggression Treaty of Neall still holds, and several wraiths serve on retainer as guides and informants.
Agents are told to avoid and flee the Society of Leopold, whose hunters seem able to find vampires anywhere; attempts to destroy it through pawns failed.

title: The Bahari in the Hand
summary: Lilith's cult within the True Hand.

claims.text: The Bahari impose purifying ordeals on wayward members and have won the trust of the Qadi.
Their temple stands in a former slave pen of Enoch; the Azicithra sect recasts Caine as son and daughter of Lilith, marked by the Serpent.
Three mortal witches Embraced by Lazarene Harbingers revived the order of the Lamia as the Drakaina.
The cult has no hierarchy of pontiffs and admits all who come sincerely to study pain, change and creation.
The Hand holds as an article of faith that the First City had no infernalists, and counts the war against diabolists among its oldest.
A shakar may go deeper into the Hand's secrets only after finding, studying and destroying an Asakku or an infernalist.

Corrupted fall when a Watcher reaches a Kindred's soul through blood and power; drinking infected blood, mind contact with a member of the path, or strong Vicissitude from a Corrupted can open the way.
The Sinister Obsession derangement needs Willpower at difficulty 8 to pursue any long goal but Vicissitude, and each Vicissitude dot adds a success to the minimum needed to avoid degeneration.
With Soul Whispers a Corrupted spends a blood point to share a tainted creature's senses and use Auspex, Animalism, Dominate and Vicissitude through it.

title: Enoch in the Underworld
summary: The First City in the Tempest.

claims.text: Enoch sits in the Tempest and opens straight onto the Labyrinth; five curved spires lift it above the sea, and Rawi poets compare them to a hand.
Soulsteel chains, still babbling, tie the spires to black marble walls; the Del'Roh forbids fire in the city.
Thousands of enslaved ghosts, lit from within by necromancy, circle the spires as false stars; members Embraced in the last century call them the Doomsday Clock.
Four sarcophagi lay on the cliff before the city arrived, wrapped in a maze of overlapping catacombs.
Inauhaten named the sleepers Loz, Arikel, Al-Marhi, Nergal and Ventru, while the Hand commonly says Loz, Nergal and Ninmgug, leaving four tombs and three or five names.
Loz brings nightmares of a helmeted warrior and lasting dread; Ninmgug's prophecies appear in blood in the library's volumes; the fourth tomb gives only a sense of being watched.
Most members hold the sleepers to be the founders of the Nosferatu, Toreador and Ventrue, though nothing supports it.

title: Inauhaten
summary: The undying caretaker of the Aralu.

claims.text: An ancient being who met the Hand in Enoch claiming to tend the Aralu; it does not seem to be Kindred and refuses to say what it is.
It remains an on-and-off ally of the Hand.

title: Ghosts as Characters
summary: Playing a wraith beside the Hand.

claims.text: Ghosts spend Pathos for blood, gaining a point per success on Manipulation + Empathy at difficulty 6 to stir an emotion in a human.
Each Generation dot a ghost buys makes it a step harder to compel by Necromancy; it is only an abstraction of potency.
The player picks three in-clan Disciplines from a list that mimics wraith powers; others need a wraith teacher. Crossing to the living world takes Auspex 5 or possession by Dominate 5.
A ghost with no fetters left is destroyed; two to four is a good number.
Not a true bloodline: Maeghar are accidents of blood mixed with fae wyrd and share no common sire; when the Kiasyd began vanishing in the Renaissance they left and dropped their old name.
Each carries a visible mark of the wyrd, from snow-white skin to extra arms, which may be bought as a Merit or Flaw.
They own little but one cherished, often grisly collection, and many drink from a cup rather than from warm skin.
The Hand gives them backup without ties, and their roaming makes them its face in the world.
